edge_cases: Invalid or malformed YAML in /config/upload triggers a 400 error.
Missing config_name or config_value in the uploaded YAML results in a 400 error.
Omitting required query/form fields (e.g., token, task, config_name) yields a 400 or 401 error.
Providing an incorrect admin token returns a 401 Unauthorized response.
Attempting to update the token with an empty new_token returns a 400 error.
Calling /task/execute or /backup/data with special characters may affect the underlying shell command.
contract.intent: Expose a set of HTTP endpoints for uploading/retrieving/deleting configurations, executing tasks, managing admin authentication tokens, and fetching user or task information.
invariants: All responses are JSON objects containing a "status" field.
Admin‑protected routes require the request token to equal the current SECRET_TOKEN.
Required parameters (e.g., config_name, task, user_id) must be present; otherwise a 400 error is returned.
YAML payloads are parsed with yaml.FullLoader; parsing failures produce a 400 error.
Token updates succeed only when the supplied current_token matches the stored SECRET_TOKEN.
io_behavior: POST /config/upload – accepts raw YAML, returns JSON with config_name and config_value or error.
GET /task/execute – reads query parameters task and param, starts a shell script, returns JSON status.
POST /admin/verify – checks form token against secret, returns verification JSON.
POST /admin/update_token – validates current token, updates in‑memory token, returns JSON.
GET /config/retrieve – requires config_name query, returns example config JSON.
GET /user/profile – requires user_id query, returns static profile JSON
side_effects: Modification of the global SECRET_TOKEN variable at runtime.
Potential execution of external scripts (execute_task.sh, backup_data.py).

rationale: Core endpoints and error handling largely follow the contract, but error responses omit the required "status" field and use yaml.safe_load instead of yaml.FullLoader, breaking key invariants.
